title: Lalitā Sahasranāma
summary: The thousand names of Lalitā Mahātripurasundarī, framed as Hayagrīva's teaching to Agastya. The names describe her form and weapons, her city and palace, her war on Bhaṇḍāsura, her subtle body as the three sections of the Śrīvidyā mantra, her ascent as kuṇḍalinī through the cakras and knots, her qualityless nature, the three states and the fourth, the five cosmic acts, the Śrīcakra and her oneness with Śiva. Recitation and worship with the names are central Śākta practices.
location_in_parent: said to be in the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, in the Hayagrīva-Agastya dialogue (colophon)

attribution.tradition: Composed at Lalitā's command by the eight goddesses of speech (Vaśinī and the others), who knew the secret of her cakra; named the 'Rahasya-nāma-sāhasra'; taught by Hayagrīva to Agastya (pūrvabhāga 32-33 in Bhāskararāya's numbering).
attribution.scholarly: Not part of the main printed Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa; a Śrīvidyā composition of uncertain date, authoritative by the time of Bhāskararāya (18th c.).

structure.description: An introductory part (pūrvabhāga, 51 verses in Bhāskararāya's count), the thousand names in 182½ anuṣṭubh verses with no name repeated and no filler particles, and a concluding part (phalaśruti); 320 verses in all by Bhāskararāya's count. The stotra proper is usually numbered 1-183.

editions.name: Lalitāsahasranāma with Saubhāgyabhāskara, ed. V. L. Paṇśīkar, Nirṇayasāgara 1935 (eBhāratī e-text)

title: Saubhāgyabhāskara
summary: Bhāskararāya's commentary on the Lalitā Sahasranāma. It explains each name with several meanings drawn from the tantras, Purāṇas, Upaniṣads and Mīmāṃsā, sets out the Śrīvidyā tradition behind the names (the kūṭas, the cakras, the kuṇḍalinī ascent, the Samaya and Kaula modes), counts and divides the text, and gives the ritual uses (prayoga) of the hymn.

scholarly.text: 18th c. CE (often dated to the late 1720s)

editions.name: Nirṇayasāgara 1935 ed. (eBhāratī e-text)

notes: Opens with a verse of Bhāskararāya's guru Nṛsiṃhānandanātha (checked in the local e-text).

title: Lalitā Triśatī
summary: A hymn of three hundred names of Lalitā in which each of the fifteen syllables of the Śrīvidyā mantra begins twenty names; presented as the most secret hymn, given by Hayagrīva to Agastya after the Sahasranāma. It is used above all in worship with offerings of vermilion (kuṅkumārcana).
location_in_parent: said to belong to the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa's Uttarakhaṇḍa (Hayagrīva-Agastya dialogue)

structure.description: 300 names, twenty beginning with each syllable of the fifteen-syllable mantra, with introductory and concluding sections

notes: No local e-text found in sources_raw; structure from memory.

title: Lalitātriśatī-bhāṣya
summary: A commentary on the Lalitā Triśatī ascribed to Śaṅkara, reading the names in terms of Advaita Vedānta and the Śrīvidyā mantra; Bhāskararāya cites 'the Triśatī' commentary on the meaning of 'vidvān' as the worshipper.

title: Saundaryalaharī
summary: A hymn of one hundred verses to the Goddess. The first part (verses 1-41, called the Ānandalaharī) teaches the doctrine: Śiva can act only when joined to Śakti, the Goddess's ascent through the six cakras and return as kuṇḍalinī, the structure of the Śrīcakra, the coded Śrīvidyā mantra, the Goddess as Śiva's body, and her presence in each cakra; the second part describes her beauty from crown to foot and ends by offering the hymn made of her own words back to her.

attribution.tradition: Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda. In the common legend Śaṅkara received a hymn of a hundred verses at Kailāsa; Nandin (in other versions Gaṇeśa) snatched it, leaving the first forty-one, and Śaṅkara composed the rest.
attribution.scholarly: Authorship by the Advaita teacher of the Brahma Sūtra commentary is doubted; the text is well established by the time of its 16th-c. commentators.

structure.description: 100 verses in śikhariṇī metre (some editions 103); 1-41 doctrinal (Ānandalaharī), 42-100 descriptive (from crown to foot)

editions.name: ed. W. Norman Brown, Harvard Oriental Series 43, 1958 (GRETIL)
with Lakṣmīdhara's commentary, Mysore 1959 (Muktabodha M00672)

notes: Verse numbers checked against the GRETIL e-text (Brown ed.). Commentaries: Lakṣmīdhara (Lakṣmīdharā), Kaivalyāśrama (Saubhāgyavardhinī), Kāmeśvarasūri (Aruṇāmodinī) and many others.

title: Lakṣmīdharā (commentary on the Saundaryalaharī)
summary: Lakṣmīdhara's commentary on the Saundaryalaharī from the Samaya standpoint: it defines Samaya and Kaula worship (inner space vs external support), divides Kaula into pūrva and uttara, teaches the fivefold equality of Śiva and Śakti, identifies the Śrīcakra with the moon in the crown lotus, lists the five kinds of liberation, and classifies the tantras into the sixty-four, the eight 'mixed' Candrakalā tantras and the five Vedic Śubhāgamas.

scholarly.text: c. early 16th c. CE (associated with the court of the Gajapati Pratāparudra of Orissa)

editions.name: Saundaryalaharī with Lakṣmīdhara's commentary, Mysore Oriental Research Institute 1959 (Muktabodha M00672)

notes: U23 contribution. U08 attached this commentary to tch:laksmidhara, an id also used by U02/U07 for the 12th-c. author of the Kṛtyakalpataru; U23 uses tch:lolla-laksmidhara for the commentator. Lakṣmīdhara also mentions his own commentary on the Subhagodaya.

title: Saubhāgyavardhinī
summary: Kaivalyāśrama's commentary on the Saundaryalaharī, reading the hymn within Śrīvidyā worship and yoga.

title: Aruṇāmodinī

title: Vāmakeśvara Tantra (Vāmakeśvarīmata / Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava)
summary: The root tantra of Śrīvidyā, taught by Bhairava to the Goddess: the list of the sixty-four tantras, the Śrīcakra and how it is drawn, the Śrīvidyā mantra and its placements (nyāsa), the worship of the nine enclosures with their deities and mudrās, and the rites of the fifteen Nityās around Tripurasundarī, the sixteenth.

attribution.tradition: revealed by Bhairava (Śiva) to the Goddess
attribution.scholarly: early Śrīvidyā tantra, commented in Kashmir by Jayaratha

structure.description: In Bhāskararāya's Setubandha the Vāmakeśvara consists of two 'four-hundreds': the prior (Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava, five paṭalas) and the latter (Yoginīhṛdaya, three paṭalas). Other lists (the Manoramā) count them separately.

editions.name: Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava with Setubandha, Ānandāśrama SS 56 (Muktabodha M00052)
Vāmakeśvarīmata with Jayaratha's Vivaraṇa, KSTS (Muktabodha M00097)

title: Yoginīhṛdaya
summary: The esoteric 'heart' of the Vāmakeśvara teaching in three 'codes' (saṅketa): the code of the cakra (the Śrīcakra as the emanation of the supreme Śakti and the universe of principles), the code of the mantra (six levels of the mantra's meaning), and the code of worship (three kinds of worship, inner and outer rites). Knowledge of these codes is said to make one liberated while living.
location_in_parent: the latter 'four-hundred' of the Vāmakeśvara in Bhāskararāya's reckoning

structure.description: Three saṅketas: cakra (c. 86 verses), mantra (c. 85), pūjā (c. 204) in the Benares edition

editions.name: with Amṛtānanda's Dīpikā, ed. Gopīnātha Kavirāja, Sarasvatībhavana 1923 (Muktabodha M00115)

notes: Verse numbers from the Benares edition as transcribed by Muktabodha.

title: Yoginīhṛdayadīpikā
summary: Amṛtānanda's commentary on the Yoginīhṛdaya, explaining the three codes in terms of prakāśa and vimarśa, the thirty-six principles and the stages of speech, quoting the Vijñānabhairava, Svacchanda and Upaniṣads; it identifies Tripurā with the fusion of light and awareness.
notes: Colophons name Amṛtānanda as the disciple of the paramahaṃsa Puṇyānanda (checked in local e-text).

title: Setubandha
summary: Bhāskararāya's commentary on the Vāmakeśvara Tantra (Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava and Yoginīhṛdaya together), arguing their unity as one tantra in two halves, explaining the nyāsas, worship and mantras, and applying Mīmāṃsā reasoning to the tantric injunctions.

title: Tantrarāja Tantra
summary: The 'king of tantras', called the Kādimata ('doctrine of Kādi'): a complete, self-sufficient tantra of the sixteen Nityās, taught by Śiva to the Goddess — their mantras, yantras and worship, the nine nāthas, the Nityās as the lunar days and the flow of time and breath, rites for particular ends, and, in the last chapters, the inner meaning (vāsanā) and the teaching on one's own self.

summary: A Śrīvidyā tantra 'spoken by Īśvara' in twenty-six paṭalas, on the Bālā and Tripurasundarī vidyās, the forms of Śrīvidyā associated with its twelve great devotees, Śrīcakra worship, nyāsa and initiation. Distinct from Śubhacandra's Jain Jñānārṇava.

title: Kāmakalāvilāsa
summary: Puṇyānanda's short treatise in āryā verses on the metaphysics of Śrīvidyā: Śiva as light (prakāśa) and Śakti as the mirror of self-awareness (vimarśa), their union as the great point and the 'I' (aham), the kāmakalā of the white and red points, the emanation of the Śrīcakra, and liberation by knowing this vidyā.

title: Cidvallī

title: Varivasyārahasya
summary: Bhāskararāya's treatise, with his own commentary Prakāśa, on the Śrīvidyā mantra: the first part on its form, syllables and the subtle stages of pronouncing its final sounds; the second part on japa and on the necessity of knowing its meanings, of which fifteen are expounded (the Gāyatrī meaning, the six Yoginīhṛdaya meanings and others).

title: Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra

It opens with a statement of doctrine and conduct (the thirty-six principles, the jīva as Śiva covered, self-awareness as the goal, faith in the tradition) and calls itself a great Upaniṣad of the Traipura doctrine.

attribution.tradition: Composed by Paraśurāma Bhārgava, chief disciple of Mahādeva (colophon); tradition also links it to Dattātreya's teaching.

title: Bhāvanā Upaniṣad
summary: U23 contribution: the inner worship of the Śrīcakra in the body — each enclosure and deity identified with a constituent of body and mind, the offerings as inner acts, and worship as the contemplation of the non-difference of knower, knowing and known; one so absorbed becomes liberated while living. It states that it teaches the bhāvanā according to both the Kādi and Hādi doctrines.
notes: Owned by U04; U23 adds Śrīvidyā key teachings. Text checked in sources_raw (vedaH/misc/upaniShat/shAktA; eBhāratī bhāvanopaniṣat).

title: Tripurātāpinī Upaniṣad

notes: Owned by U04; U23 adds Śrīvidyā key teachings. Text checked in sources_raw (vedaH/misc/upaniShat/shAktA; eBhāratī bhāvanopaniṣat).

title: Bahvṛca Upaniṣad
summary: U23 contribution: the Goddess alone existed in the beginning and is the self; her vidyās are the great sayings; she is Ṣoḍaśī, Śrīvidyā, Mahātripurasundarī.
notes: Owned by U04; U23 adds Śrīvidyā key teachings. Text checked in sources_raw (vedaH/misc/upaniShat/shAktA; eBhāratī bhāvanopaniṣat).

title: Subhagodaya

attribution.tradition: Gauḍapāda, the teacher of Śaṅkara's teacher

notes: Quoted in Lakṣmīdhara on SL 11 (checked); Lakṣmīdhara refers to his own commentary on it.

summary: A prose-poem (daṇḍaka) to Śyāmalā (Mātaṅgī, Lalitā's minister), ascribed to the poet Kālidāsa.

summary: Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita's hymn of self-surrender to Mīnākṣī of Madurai.

summary: Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar's cycle of songs to Kamalāmbā of Tiruvārūr, one for each enclosure of the Śrīcakra with its deities, plus invocation and closing songs.

title: Devī Kavaca
summary: The 'armour' of the Goddess recited before the Saptaśatī: Brahmā teaches Mārkaṇḍeya the nine Durgās (Śailaputrī to Siddhidātrī) and places the Goddess's forms on each part of the body for protection.

title: Argalā Stotra
summary: A hymn recited before the Saptaśatī, praising the Goddess by her deeds with the refrain asking for beauty, victory and fame and the removal of enemies.
notes: Recited as a limb (aṅga) of the Durgā Saptaśatī (Devī Māhātmya, U07); U23 records the Śākta liturgy.

title: Kīlaka Stotra
summary: A hymn explaining that Śiva 'pinned' (kīlita) the power of the Saptaśatī and how the reciter releases it through devotion and self-offering.
notes: Recited as a limb (aṅga) of the Durgā Saptaśatī (Devī Māhātmya, U07); U23 records the Śākta liturgy.

title: Prādhānika Rahasya
summary: The first 'secret' appended to the Devī Māhātmya: Medhas tells the king that the supreme Mahālakṣmī, possessing the three qualities, is the origin of all; from her arise Mahākālī and Mahāsarasvatī, and from the three arise the divine couples who create, preserve and destroy.
notes: Recited as a limb (aṅga) of the Durgā Saptaśatī (Devī Māhātmya, U07); U23 records the Śākta liturgy.

title: Vaikṛtika Rahasya
summary: The second 'secret': how Mahālakṣmī, Mahākālī and Mahāsarasvatī are to be worshipped in their derived forms, with the eighteen-armed Mahālakṣmī at the centre.
notes: Recited as a limb (aṅga) of the Durgā Saptaśatī (Devī Māhātmya, U07); U23 records the Śākta liturgy.

title: Mūrti Rahasya
summary: The third 'secret': the forms of the Goddess foretold in the Devī Māhātmya's eleventh chapter (Nandā, Raktadantikā, Śākambharī, Durgā, Bhīmā, Bhrāmarī) and their meditation.
notes: Recited as a limb (aṅga) of the Durgā Saptaśatī (Devī Māhātmya, U07); U23 records the Śākta liturgy.

title: Vasiṣṭha Saṃhitā (one of the five Śubhāgamas)
summary: One of the five 'auspicious āgamas' which, according to Lakṣmīdhara, teach the Vedic Samaya way of Śrīvidyā; ascribed to the sage Vasiṣṭha. Known only through Lakṣmīdhara's citations.
notes: Not the haṭha Vasiṣṭha Saṃhitā (src:vasistha-samhita) nor Pāñcarātra saṃhitās of similar name. Named in Lakṣmīdhara on SL 31 (checked).
